question: Should OpenClaw support a broad config-driven Tailnet/private-ingress mode that disables Gateway token URL auth, HTTPS expectations, device identity, and pairing, or should this remain rejected in core?
rationale: The request intentionally moves Gateway protection from OpenClaw-managed auth and pairing to operator-owned network controls, which is a security boundary and product policy decision automation cannot make.

options.title: Keep Safe Defaults
options.body: Continue rejecting broad no-auth Tailnet exposure and point users to token/password, verified Tailscale WebSocket identity, trusted-proxy auth, or the narrower no-auth policy discussion.

options.title: Sponsor Dangerous Opt-In
options.body: Design an explicit private-ingress or Tailnet-trusted mode with scary naming, startup warnings, audit findings, docs, and focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: If maintainers reject this trust model in core, close this issue and related satellites with a clear supported-alternatives comment.

recommendation.title: Keep Safe Defaults
recommendation.body: Continue rejecting broad no-auth Tailnet exposure and point users to token/password, verified Tailscale WebSocket identity, trusted-proxy auth, or the narrower no-auth policy discussion.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent history across Gateway auth hardening, Tailscale auth, and the adjacent no-auth exposure fix.
